title: Governmental Accounting Final Review
description: Review governmental fund reporting, measurement focus, basis of accounting, and government-wide concepts.
html:
The Big Governmental Accounting Split

Governmental accounting becomes much easier when you first identify which financial statements you are dealing with.

GOVERNMENT-WIDE STATEMENTS → ECONOMIC RESOURCES + ACCRUAL ACCOUNTING GOVERNMENTAL FUND STATEMENTS → CURRENT FINANCIAL RESOURCES + MODIFIED ACCRUAL

Government-Wide Financial Statements

Government-wide statements provide a broad economic view of governmental and business-type activities.

GOVERNMENT-WIDE: STATEMENT OF NET POSITION STATEMENT OF ACTIVITIES

These statements generally include long-term assets and long-term liabilities.

Governmental Fund Statements

Governmental funds focus on current financial resources rather than the government's total economic resources.

GOVERNMENTAL FUND: BALANCE SHEET + STATEMENT OF REVENUES, EXPENDITURES, AND CHANGES IN FUND BALANCES

Governmental Funds

The governmental fund category includes:

GENERAL FUND SPECIAL REVENUE FUNDS CAPITAL PROJECTS FUNDS DEBT SERVICE FUNDS PERMANENT FUNDS

General Fund

The General Fund accounts for resources not required to be reported in another fund.

GENERAL FUND → DEFAULT GOVERNMENTAL FUND

Special Revenue Fund

Special revenue funds generally account for proceeds of specific revenue sources restricted or committed to specified purposes other than debt service or capital projects.

Capital Projects Fund

Capital projects funds generally account for financial resources that are restricted, committed, or assigned for capital outlays, including the acquisition or construction of capital facilities and other capital assets.

Debt Service Fund

Debt service funds generally account for resources accumulated and used for principal and interest payments on general long-term debt.

Permanent Fund

Permanent funds account for resources for which the principal generally must remain intact while earnings may be used for governmental purposes.

Modified Accrual Revenue Recognition

Under modified accrual accounting, governmental fund revenue is generally recognized when it is both:

MEASURABLE + AVAILABLE → RECOGNIZE REVENUE

Available generally means collectible soon enough to finance expenditures of the current period.

Example — Property Tax Revenue

Assume a governmental fund levies $1,000,000 of property taxes.

At year-end:

Amount measurable: $1,000,000

Amount considered available: $940,000

REVENUE RECOGNIZED = $940,000

The portion not considered available is not recognized as current-period governmental fund revenue merely because it is measurable.

Expenditures vs Expenses

Governmental fund statements report expenditures, while government-wide statements report expenses.

GOVERNMENTAL FUND → EXPENDITURES GOVERNMENT-WIDE → EXPENSES

Capital Asset Purchase

This is one of the most important governmental accounting differences.

Suppose a government purchases equipment for $300,000.

GOVERNMENTAL FUND: CAPITAL OUTLAY EXPENDITURE = $300,000
GOVERNMENT-WIDE: CAPITAL ASSET = $300,000 THEN DEPRECIATE OVER USEFUL LIFE

Long-Term Debt Issuance

Governmental funds generally do not report general long-term debt as a fund liability.

Instead, proceeds from issuance of general long-term debt are generally reported as an other financing source in the governmental fund.

GOVERNMENTAL FUND: BOND PROCEEDS → OTHER FINANCING SOURCE GOVERNMENT-WIDE: BOND ISSUANCE → LONG-TERM LIABILITY

Example — Bond Issuance

A city issues $2,000,000 of general obligation bonds.

Governmental Fund $2,000,000 Other Financing Source
Government-Wide $2,000,000 Liability

Debt Principal Payments

In governmental funds, payment of general long-term debt principal is generally reported as an expenditure.

GOVERNMENTAL FUND PRINCIPAL PAYMENT → EXPENDITURE GOVERNMENT-WIDE PRINCIPAL PAYMENT → REDUCE LIABILITY

Interest on Long-Term Debt

Governmental funds generally recognize expenditures for general long-term debt interest when the related obligation becomes due, subject to applicable governmental accounting guidance.

Government-wide statements use accrual accounting and recognize interest expense as incurred.

Encumbrances

Encumbrance accounting is a budgetary control mechanism often associated with governmental accounting.

A purchase order can create an encumbrance, helping prevent governments from committing resources beyond authorized amounts.

PURCHASE ORDER → ENCUMBRANCE GOODS / SERVICES RECEIVED → REVERSE ENCUMBRANCE + RECORD ACTUAL EXPENDITURE AND LIABILITY

An outstanding encumbrance by itself is not the same thing as a recognized expenditure or liability.

Proprietary Funds

Proprietary funds use accounting similar to business enterprises.

PROPRIETARY FUNDS → ECONOMIC RESOURCES + ACCRUAL ACCOUNTING

The two major proprietary fund types are:

ENTERPRISE FUND INTERNAL SERVICE FUND

Enterprise Funds

Enterprise funds generally report activities financed primarily through charges to external users for goods or services.

COMMON EXAMPLES: WATER UTILITY PUBLIC TRANSIT SYSTEM MUNICIPAL AIRPORT

Internal Service Funds

Internal service funds generally account for goods or services provided primarily to other departments or agencies of the same government.

Fiduciary Activities

Fiduciary activities involve resources the government holds for others and that meet the applicable fiduciary criteria.

Fiduciary funds use:

ECONOMIC RESOURCES + ACCRUAL ACCOUNTING

Fiduciary activities generally are not included in government-wide governmental or business-type activities because those resources are held for others.

Government-Wide Classification

GOVERNMENTAL ACTIVITIES + BUSINESS-TYPE ACTIVITIES

Fiduciary activities are excluded from these government-wide activity columns.

Fund Balance Categories

Governmental fund balance may be classified into several categories based on the nature of constraints placed on the resources.

NONSPENDABLE RESTRICTED COMMITTED ASSIGNED UNASSIGNED

Nonspendable

Resources are nonspendable when they cannot be spent because of their form or because they are legally or contractually required to remain intact.

Restricted

Restricted fund balance results from externally enforceable constraints or qualifying legal restrictions.

Committed

Committed amounts are constrained for a specific purpose by the government's highest level of decision-making authority.

Assigned

Assigned amounts represent intended uses of resources that do not meet the stricter criteria for restricted or committed classification.

Unassigned

Unassigned fund balance generally represents residual spendable resources available for purposes not otherwise constrained.

Reconciliation Is Critical

Governmental fund statements and government-wide statements use different measurement focuses and bases of accounting.

Therefore, reconciliation is required.

GOVERNMENTAL FUND BALANCE + CAPITAL ASSETS − ACCUMULATED DEPRECIATION − LONG-TERM LIABILITIES ± OTHER CONVERSION ITEMS = GOVERNMENTAL ACTIVITIES NET POSITION

Example — Simple Reconciliation

Governmental fund balance: $900,000

Capital assets, net: $2,400,000

General long-term debt: $1,500,000

$900,000 + $2,400,000 − $1,500,000 = $1,800,000 GOVERNMENTAL ACTIVITIES NET POSITION

Conversion Logic

FUND STATEMENTS DO NOT REPORT GENERAL CAPITAL ASSETS → ADD THEM FUND STATEMENTS DO NOT REPORT GENERAL LONG-TERM LIABILITIES → SUBTRACT THEM

Capital Outlay Conversion

A governmental fund reports the entire cost of a capital asset as an expenditure.

At the government-wide level, however, the asset is capitalized and depreciation expense is recognized over time.

FUND EXPENDITURE → REMOVE FOR GOVERNMENT-WIDE PURPOSES CAPITALIZE ASSET + RECOGNIZE DEPRECIATION

Bond Proceeds Conversion

Governmental fund bond proceeds are other financing sources.

At the government-wide level, issuing debt does not create revenue.

REMOVE OTHER FINANCING SOURCE + RECORD LIABILITY

FAR Governmental Strategy

FIRST QUESTION: FUND LEVEL OR GOVERNMENT-WIDE? THEN ASK: WHAT MEASUREMENT FOCUS? WHAT BASIS OF ACCOUNTING? REVENUE OR OTHER FINANCING SOURCE? EXPENDITURE OR EXPENSE? CAPITAL ASSET REPORTED? LONG-TERM DEBT REPORTED?

Key Takeaways

  • Governmental funds use the current financial resources measurement focus and modified accrual accounting.
  • Government-wide statements use the economic resources measurement focus and accrual accounting.
  • Governmental fund revenue generally must be measurable and available.
  • General capital asset purchases are expenditures at the governmental fund level but assets at the government-wide level.
  • General long-term bond proceeds are generally other financing sources in governmental funds but liabilities at the government-wide level.
  • Proprietary and fiduciary funds use accrual accounting and an economic resources measurement focus.
  • Encumbrances help control spending but are not automatically liabilities or expenditures.
  • Reconciliations explain the differences between governmental fund reporting and government-wide reporting.

quiz.prompt: A city issues $2,000,000 of general obligation bonds to finance construction of a public building. How should the bond proceeds generally be reported in the city's governmental fund statements?
quiz.explanation: Governmental funds focus on current financial resources and generally do not report general long-term debt as a fund liability. Proceeds from issuing general long-term debt are generally reported as an other financing source. At the government-wide level, the bonds are reported as a liability.
